source.title: Gated Attention Blocks: Preliminary Progress toward Removing Attention Head Superposition

record.tranche_reason: The study tests attention-head superposition in toy networks, not neuron polysemanticity or any of the listed neuron-focused versions. Its discussion of neuron polysemanticity is background rather than a tested result.
record.gate_note: The study reports results about attention heads, a related but different construct from the claim's neuron-focused versions. It cites neuron polysemanticity as background but does not test it. The attention-head results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study builds a gated attention block to remove attention-head superposition in toy attention-only models. It measures no neurons: no MLP or vision neurons, and no polysemanticity rates. It mentions neuron polysemanticity (citing Gurnee et al.) only as background. Attention-head superposition is a related but different construct, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that gated attention blocks resolve OV-Incoherent attention-head superposition in toy setups, so each representation can be assigned to one head. They leave larger models and other forms of superposition to future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a modified, expanded gated attention block with a sparsity penalty on toy OV-Incoherent skip-trigram tasks. It does not use a neuron-polysemanticity measurement or the methods of the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report anecdotally that an L0.6 coefficient set too high prevented representations from being learned, while one set too low did not remove attention-head superposition. They did not perform a robust hyperparameter sweep.

fits_no_version.finding: In toy single-layer attention-only models, some OV-Incoherent skip trigrams are encoded across several heads. A gated attention block with an L0.6 sparsity penalty and a 2x head expansion reassigned each tested trigram to a single head.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attention blocks can represent more skip-trigram behaviours than they have heads via cross-head superposition, and gated sparse blocks can resolve this in toy settings.

record.problems: The experiments use toy, single-layer attention-only models with one-hot (un)embeddings and no layer norm or positional embeddings. They examine only OV-Incoherent attention-head superposition. The authors note limited hyperparameter sweeps, inadequate controls against an expanded traditional block or a gated block without sparsity, and that low reconstruction loss does not establish equivalent internal behaviour. Uncertainty estimates are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No further separately described result rows were available in the text. Figures are referenced but their visual contents and any additional numerical details are not present in the supplied text.

untested.parts: all; no vision models are studied
all; no MLP neurons are measured
all; the study covers superposition across attention heads only, not neurons
all; the gated block targets head superposition, not the share of polysemantic neurons

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong post from MATS. Its only link to neuron polysemanticity is background citation. The post also mentions possibly reducing attention-head polysemanticity, but leaves this unexplored.

versions.untested_parts: No image-classifier neurons or vision inputs are examined.
No MLP neurons in language models or token/context response patterns are measured.
The study does not test whether neuron polysemanticity is caused by superposition or capacity pressure.
The study does not test neuron polysemanticity arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise without capacity pressure.
The study does not measure neuron polysemanticity across activation functions, architectures, or regularization settings, or its effect on performance.
The study does not investigate whether apparently polysemantic neurons detect shared features or related jobs.
The study does not test how measurements or explanation scoring affect whether a neuron counts as polysemantic.

rows.subject: gated attention block trained to match the single-layer 4-head model

rows.note: The authors report that the gated block removed the tested attention-head superposition in this setup.
